newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares set course to break 3,800 in DAX.
newsitem.headline: German shares set course to break 3,800 in DAX.

text.p: German shares raced to early gains in bourse dealings on Friday and held on to most of the advance in moderate activity tied to the "triple witching" expiry of DAX futures, DAX options and stock options.
The 30-share DAX index ended bourse trade at a new record high, rising 39 points to 3,788.27 points, and after also reaching a new record high at 3,798.94.
The IBIS DAX, which reflects all-day computer trade, was up 5.17 points at 3,782.73 in post-bourse dealings after reaching a new high at 3,801.35 during the bourse trading session.

"The expiration was relatively quiet and the market remains very supportive at these levels," said one Frankfurt trader. "I would expect the DAX to keep the gains for today. We also have a good chance of ending above 3,800 points."
The DAX index shot higher at the outset, getting a boost from overnight Wall Street gains and the firmer dollar as well as traders unwinding options positions.
Modest gains in German debt futures, which briefly fell in morning trade after German M3 money supply rose an annualised 7.0 percent in May, also helped the share market advance.

The DAX futures contract, which ended trade on Thursday at 3,777.0 points, was given a final settlement price at 3,801.85 points at the start on Friday, underpinning sentiment and pushing the DAX index higher throughout the session.
But sell orders, including some from foreign institutional investors, in the last 10 minutes of trade pared gains in the DAX index, traders said.
They noted that the DAX closed below the final level for settlement of DAX options, which was pegged at 3,795 points based on the average trading range for the last 10 minutes.
"The market is still in very good shape," said one trader. "This was a relatively harmless expiry."
Dealings in the afternoon will focus on Wall Street, which has been the driving factor for the German share market.
"The market right now is more focussed on the U.S. right now instead of on domestic factors," said another trader.

Away from the expiry helping the market, traders said the dollar stabilising above 1.70 marks helped support the advance based on views that dollar-sensitive shares would benefit, in turn helping the export-led German recovery.

Among specific shares, retailer Karstadt AG advanced ahead of the market, ending up 16.50 marks at 642 marks after falling on Thursday when holding group WCM said it was not interested in buying a stake in Karstadt.
SGL Carbon, which said last week it was the focus of a class-action lawsuit in the United States over price-fixing allegations, rose 11 marks to 233 marks in a recovery from recent heavy losses.
